page.layout: One printed page of text. Above the text: two round coin medallions with legends, each carrying the name of a king. Below the text: a woodcut ornament (no text). No margin notes.

main_text.p: OZIAS, qui & Azarias, filius Amasiæ, constitutus est Rex Iudæ ab vniuerso populo, & in locum patris subrogatus annos tantum natus sedecim. Cœpit itaque regnare viuo patre, anno mundi 3124. ante Christum natum 838. imperauit 52. annis: nempe 11. viuo patre, aduersus quem coniuratum fuerat: deinde 41. annos post patrem occisum. Hic initio pius, auxilioque diuino fretus, Philisthæos, Arabes, Ammonitas deuicit, tributarios fecit: ciuitatem Ierusalem restaurauit: tandem ex opulentia in superbiam lapsus, dum sacerdotis munus vsurpat, volens sacrificare atque adolere incensum super altare, dumque sacerdotibus ipsum corripientibus minatur, in lepram incidit: atque à sacerdotibus è templo pellitur: manfitque leprosus ad obitum vsque. successit ei Ioathan. Vide lib.4. Reg.14. & 15.cap. & 2.lib.Paral.26.cap. Item Iosep.lib.Anti.9.cap.11.

IOATHAN filius Oziæ seu Azatiæ, Regis Iudæ, succef-fit patri, eodem in regno, anno secundo Phaceæ filij Romeliæ Regis Israel: qui erat annus mundi 3176. ante Christum natum 786. Hic pietatem coluit: portam domus Domini excelsam ædificauit: vrbes quoque in montibus Iuda, & in saltibus castella & turres. pugnauit contra Regem filiorum Ammon, quem vicit, fecitque tributarium. imperauit annis 16. & succef-fit ei filius eius Achas. Videto vt supra.

page.notes: The two medallion legends are printed on the coins and are transcribed as lines; the right-hand coin's left legend reads "RI", cut off by the frame. Long s has been written as plain s. The line-end break "succef-" / "fit" keeps its printed hyphen. Azatiæ is as printed; the reading is clear but may be a printing variant of Azariæ. The faint ghost text below the second paragraph is show-through from the reverse and is left out. The woodcut ornament at the foot carries no text.
